businessModel: Freeware, free for personal and commercial use; donation page; revenue sources such as search partnerships are not documented
updateCadence: Major Chromium migration roughly every 3-6 months (48.0 Oct 2025, 50.0 Apr 2026, 51.0 Oct 2026) with point releases between; the FAQ promises a lag of no more than three months
summary: FlashPeak's freeware Chromium browser adds an ad blocker, a YouTube video downloader, a side tab bar and an AI chat panel, with Chrome Web Store compatibility. Its Chromium base lags Chrome by several months.
bestFor: Windows users who want Chrome-style browsing with built-in ad blocking
People who want a one-click video downloader and a parallel download manager
notFor: Anyone who wants Chrome-level security patch speed
People who need verified privacy: Google-service connections are disputed

pros.title: Built-in ad blocker
pros.detail: Ships with EasyList pre-loaded, with per-site disable options; a 51.0.2.0 note says its performance was improved.

pros.title: YouTube video downloader
pros.detail: Saves videos in several resolutions and can extract MP3 audio.

pros.title: Chrome extension compatibility
pros.detail: Slimjet says it supports almost all Chrome extensions and all Chrome themes from the Chrome Web Store.

pros.title: Extra convenience tools
pros.detail: Side tab bar, auto-reload, idle background tab closing and an AI Chat side panel (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Deepseek, Grok).

pros.title: Wide OS reach
pros.detail: Windows 7+, macOS 10.9+ and several Linux distributions, per the FAQ.

cons.title: Chromium lag
cons.detail: 51.0.0.0 moved to Chromium 149 in Oct 2026 while Chrome 156 shipped Oct 20, so Chrome security fixes arrive months late.

cons.title: Disputed privacy claims
cons.detail: Slimjet says no usage data goes to Google, but one tester reports Google service connections, and anonymous usage statistics are on by default (can be disabled).

cons.title: Proprietary and thinly documented
cons.detail: Source is not published and the release log has no dates; the blog has no 2026 posts.

cons.title: No native Apple silicon or mobile apps
cons.detail: The Mac build runs through Rosetta per a download-site listing, and there are no Android or iOS versions.

faq.a: It is a Chromium build with a sandbox, but its base trails Chrome by months, so it misses recent security fixes. Keep it updated and avoid sensitive logins if you need fast patches.

faq.q: Does Slimjet send data to Google?
faq.a: Slimjet says it sends no data to Google unless you sync with a Google account; it collects anonymous usage stats you can switch off. A third-party tester disputes the Google claim.
Yes, per Slimjet, from the Chrome Web Store. Because the base is a recent Chromium, Manifest V2 extensions such as full uBlock Origin are not expected to work.
